questions.question: Where are blind spots located on flat side mirrors?

options.text: Immediately below
In the middle of
Above
To the left of

questions.correctAnswerText: Immediately below
questions.explanation: Blind spots exist immediately below and in front of each outside flat mirror. There is also a blind spot directly behind the rear bumper.

questions.question: What should a properly adjusted flat mirror show the driver?

options.text: The rear tires touching the ground.
The front tires touching the ground.
Only the roadway and no parts of the bus.
The front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear tires touching the ground.
questions.explanation: A properly adjusted flat mirror should show 200 feet behind the bus, the base of each rear wheel, and the sides of the bus.

questions.question: What should you do if a parent asks you to change a bus stop location?

options.text: Agree and pick up students at the new bus stop.
Continue to pick up students at the original bus stop.
Change the bus stop if the new location fits into your route.
Use both locations as bus stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to pick up students at the original bus stop.
questions.explanation: Bus drivers cannot change bus stop locations. Only school district officials can decide where bus stops are located.

questions.question: What should the driver do while students board the bus?

options.text: Read a book.
Check all mirrors.
Only look at the students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check all mirrors.
questions.explanation: While students board, watch all mirrors for students running to catch the bus and supervise the loading.

questions.question: What is the inside rearview mirror used for?

options.text: See passengers.
See potential hazards on the road.
See vehicles trying to switch lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: See passengers.
questions.explanation: The inside rearview mirror is used to watch what passengers are doing inside the bus.

questions.question: What should you do if a railroad crossing gate does not go up after a train passes?

options.text: Drive around the gate.
Wait for another vehicle to cross the tracks first to see if it is safe.
Call your dispatcher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call your dispatcher.
questions.explanation: If a gate stays down after a train passes, call your dispatcher. Do not drive around the lowered gate.

questions.question: When should you back up at a student pick-up point?

options.text: Back up before the students load the bus.
Let the students load the bus before backing up.
Let half of the students load the bus and then back up to meet the second half.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the students load the bus before backing up.
questions.explanation: Do not back up until all students have boarded. Always watch for students who arrive late.

questions.question: When should outside mirrors be adjusted on a school bus?

options.text: Before a trip begins.
During a trip.
After students board the bus.
After a trip ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before a trip begins.
questions.explanation: Check and adjust all mirrors before starting a trip. Proper mirror adjustment is critical for the safety of students and other vehicles.

questions.question: What is true about loading a school bus?

options.text: It is not a dangerous process.
It does not need to be supervised.
It should be done quickly.
It can be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: More students are killed during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. Bus drivers must follow safety procedures during these times.

questions.question: What should a student do if they drop an item while approaching the bus?

options.text: Stop and pick up the object.
Have another student pick up the object.
Ask the driver to pick up the object.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick up the object.
questions.explanation: If a student bends down to pick up a dropped item, the driver may not see them. This is dangerous. Instead, students should move to a safe spot away from the bus, get the driver's attention, and let the driver pick up the item.

questions.question: If a bus must be evacuated, where is it safest for students to stand?

options.text: No more than 50 feet away from the bus.
Downwind of the bus in case of a fire.
Far away from any railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Far away from any railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: After leaving a school bus, students should go to a safe place at least 100 feet away from the road. They should stand upwind from any fire and as far from railroad tracks as possible. This keeps them safe from other vehicles and debris.

questions.question: If a driver needs to leave a school bus to check on students, what should the driver do?

options.text: Leave the bus running.
Turn off the bus and take the key with them.
Ask a student to watch the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the bus and take the key with them.
questions.explanation: When the driver leaves the bus to find a missing student, they must turn off the engine and take the key. Then they should check around and under the bus for the student.

questions.question: When properly adjusted, what should the flat mirrors on a school bus show?

options.text: The sides of the bus.
The ground under the bus.
The front tires touching the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: The sides of the bus.
questions.explanation: Flat mirrors that are properly adjusted show the sides of the bus. They also let the driver see 200 feet behind the bus and the base of each rear wheel.

questions.question: Why is the area to the left of a school bus especially dangerous for students?

options.text: The sun reflects off the left side of the bus.
Other vehicles pass on the left side of the bus.
It is hard to see the left side of any bus.
There is no door on the left side of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other vehicles pass on the left side of the bus.
questions.explanation: The left side of a school bus is very dangerous because passing vehicles are there. All sides of a bus have danger zones, but the left side is the most hazardous for students.

questions.question: If your bus stalls on railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Get everyone off the bus and move far away from it.
Keep everyone on the bus and try to signal the train to stop.
Keep everyone on the bus and wait for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get everyone off the bus and move far away from it.
questions.explanation: If a school bus stalls on railroad tracks, get everyone off the bus immediately. Move away from the tracks at an angle, in the direction of any oncoming train.

questions.question: When dropping off students at school, what should a driver do?

options.text: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
Leave the key in the ignition when leaving the driver's seat.
Read a book while students get off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
questions.explanation: When students are getting off at school, turn off the engine to secure the bus. If you leave the driver's seat, remove the key from the ignition. You must watch students while they unload.

questions.question: When students are picked up by a school bus, where should they wait?

options.text: At a designated bus stop.
Anywhere the driver can reach them.
Wherever parents decide.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a designated bus stop.
questions.explanation: A school bus driver must pick up and drop off students only at stops that are approved by the school district.

questions.question: What are active railroad crossings?

options.text: Crossings that have traffic control devices.
Crossings with no traffic control devices.
Crossings used by at least 10 vehicles every hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossings that have traffic control devices.
questions.explanation: Active railroad crossings have control devices like flashing red lights, bells, and gates. Drivers must follow the instructions from these devices.

questions.question: Where should students stay during most emergencies?

options.text: On the bus
On the side of the road near the bus
In a field away from the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: On the bus
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safer and easier to control if they stay on the bus. However, if staying on the bus puts them at risk, the driver should take them to a safe place.

questions.question: Where is the overhead rearview mirror located on a school bus?

options.text: On the right side of the bus.
On the steering wheel.
Above the windshield inside the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. The driver uses it to watch the students on the bus.
